Issues.Title: Do not activate the window when applying the new DPI scale
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #7561 — a WPF window is unexpectedly activated when the system DPI changes.

`HwndTarget.OnDpiChanged` calls `SetWindowPos` to apply the new window size/position at the new DPI scale, but did not pass `SWP_NOACTIVATE`. Per the [SetWindowPos docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowpos), without that flag the window is activated and moved to the top of its Z-order group — so an inactive WPF window becomes active whenever the DPI changes.

This change adds `SWP_NOACTIVATE` to that call, matching the sibling `OnDpiChangedAfterParent` method in the same file, which already passes it.

## Verification

- Repro from the issue: create an empty WPF app, deactivate the main window (activate another window), change the system DPI. Previously the main window was activated; with this change it stays inactive.
- The sibling path (`OnDpiChangedAfterParent`, child HWND DPI change) was already correct and is untouched.

Issues.Body:
Branch [release/9.0](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/commits/release/9.0/) in `dotnet/wpf` repo can't be mirrored from GitHub to Azure [internal/release/9.0](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-wpf?version=GBinternal%2Frelease%2F9.0&_a=history) via internal merge. 

There are conflicting commits in the target branch.
The branch is configured to be mirrored via automated merge. 
The situation is rare but normal. The target branch is expected to receive manual commits in the Azure DevOps clone, which could cause conflict.

Conflicts need to be **resolved to unblock the code flow**.

- you can resolve the issue by resolving the conflict in the **target branch only**. 
    - Please make sure that the changes sensitive from security perspective are not published ahead of time to GitHub!
- reverting the extra commits in the Azdo target branch.
- checking the logs of the mirroring process in the [mirroring pipeline](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build?definitionId=1387).
- you can disable the mirroring of the branch in the [configuration file](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/dnceng-subscriptions.jsonc).
- you can ask @dotnet/dnceng for help or read the [documentation](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/README.md).

Please close this issue once the conflict is resolved.

Issues.Title: Fluent theme: maximized window's title bar covers the top of the client area
Issues.Body: ### Description With the Fluent theme on Windows 11, when a window is maximized and **Settings > Personalization > Colors > Show accent color on title bars and window borders** is on, DWM draws the title bar too tall. It covers the top ~6px of the client area. The caption buttons are also drawn 4px lower than usual. It's only visible when the top of the client area is transparent, like a toolbar or a title area without its own background. Normally the overlapping part is Mica on Mica, so it can't be seen. The cause seems to be that `WindowBackdropManager.UpdateGlassFrame` extends the frame into the client area with all margins set to -1. For a maximized window, DWM then fills the title bar at its non-maximized height. https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/blob/main/src/Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf/src/PresentationFramework/System/Windows/Appearance/WindowBackdropManager.cs#L126-L131 ### Reproduction Steps A minimal repro project is attached (FluentMaximizedCaptionRepro.zip). It's a new WPF app with `ThemeMode="Light"`, a maximized window, and a 2px red line at the top of the client area. 1. On Windows 11 22H2 or later, turn on **Settings > Personalization > Colors > Show accent color on title bars and window borders**. 2. Run the attached project (`dotnet run`). 3. Make sure the window is active (the accent color is only used for the active window's title bar). [FluentMaximizedCaptionRepro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35222870/FluentMaximizedCaptionRepro.zip) ### Expected behavior The title bar ends where the client area starts (at the red line), like a non-Fluent window. ### Actual behavior The accent-colored title bar continues ~6px below the red line, behind the window content (the red line itself is drawn on top of it). Before / after the workaround (100% scale): ### Regression? Not a regression. The Fluent window backdrop was added in .NET 9. ### Known Workarounds AI-suggested workaround/fix: Extend the frame from the bottom only (`cyBottomHeight` = a large value, other margins 0) which still covers the whole client area, so the backdrop still shows there, and DWM draws the title bar at the correct height. Re-applying the margins from app code works, but WPF resets them on every theme change and WM_SETTINGCHANGE, so a WPF change would be better. ### Impact Moderate: affects any Fluent-themed app with transparent content at the top of a maximized window, for users with accent-colored title bars. ### Configuration - .NET 10.0.15 (also reproduced on .NET 11.0.0) - Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200), x64 (also reproduced on 26H2) ### Other information _No response_

Issues.Title: Hide edges from IME during SetText
Issues.Body:
Fixes #3630 

/cc @pranav-gupta-msft @amarinov-msft 

## Description

The issue is that some edits require changes to the document structure. In #3630, such edit is inserting text in front of the first `BlockUIContainer`, which needs to insert a Paragraph there to hold the text. When the edit comes from an IME, we are under lock in which we are not allowed to announce changes to the document. IME has two ways to request edit: `InsertTextAtSelection` and `SetText`. The former API has a structure allowing us to communicate back to the IME the changes we had to do. `SetText` does not. The current behavior then is we do the necessary changes, cannot tell anyone, character offsets get out of sync and we fail fast when we find out. "Characters" here includes special characters representing a start of an element in a document ("left edge").

The fix is we hide the newly created elements from the IME (defer their edges) until we are allowed to announce changes, at which point we raise the normal events about document changes. A tree keeps a track of list of elements that have an deferred edge.

All new code reachable from `SetText` has previously caused crash, no existing behavior should be changed.

Now `InsertTextAtSelection` includes change in behavior that is strictly not required to fix the crash. When the fix is taken, non-IME typing and `SetText` behave the same - when you type over a selection, the selection is replaced as expected. That is not currently the case with `InsertTextAtSelection` which collapses the selection first (or in same cases rejects the edit). That seems wrong, so I aligned the behavior with the other two methods, but again all unaffected scenarios should go through existing code path.

Finally, when user types something through IME and we have to create a Paragraph for it, cancelling the composition does not remove the inserted Paragraph. This is similar to typing without IME where backspace also does not remove the inserted Paragraph. It is possible to keep track of the implicit Paragraph and automatically remove it when composition is cancelled, but it was too much extra code for minimal benefit.

This is one of the more complex parts of WPF and I am not married to the solution. If anyone has better suggestions how to address this (I tried several), chime in.

## Customer Impact

Without this fix, customer applications will crash / fail fast with `ExecutionEngineException` whenever typing using IME when the cursor is at a `BlockUIContainer` boundary.

## Regression

No. Repros in .NET Framework.

## Testing

Tested few scenarios using Microsoft rule-based TSF (Tamil Anjali) including the case in #3630 which crashes without the fix and does not crash with the fix. I also tested it with voice input, as some code paths do not execute when typing on keyboard (namely if there is a preexisting selection, TSF first calls TestKeyDown, which translates into our OnPreviewKeyDown, where we find out we have a selection, we delete it, tell the IME, which sees it as a conflict and does not start a composition - voice does not send key downs).

Tested using locally built WPF x64 using 12.0.100-alpha.1.26569.103 SDK.

It needs to be said that there is a lot of test cases and it is very likely I missed some. I think typing over pre-selected Tables still causes a crash, and I think IME trying to insert new lines into Hyperlnk will cause crash, but I haven't tested those as that is not related to the reported issue.

## Risk

All new and changed code should execute only in a specific case - the caret or selection touches a BlockUIContainer edge. Most of the new code only runs in scenarios where we currently crash. Slight change of behavior when IME types over selection using `InsertTextAtSelection` to align it with other methods of input (and the expectation that typing over a selection replaces it).

Issues.Title: [WriteableBitmap] Retain the _lockCount == 0 guard so subscription and notification occur only after the final unlock
Issues.Body:
Fixes #4396
Addresses review comment https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/pull/4425#discussion_r4524764906

## Description

Restore the `_lockCount == 0` guard in `WriteableBitmap.SubscribeToCommittingBatchAndWritePostscript`, as suggested in dotnet/wpf#4425.

This ensures commit subscription and `Changed` notification occur only after the final `Unlock()`, rather than while nested locks remain outstanding.

## Customer Impact

Applications using nested `WriteableBitmap` locks could trigger premature change notifications and rendering while the back buffer is still locked, violating the rendering path's zero-lock-count invariant.

## Regression

Addresses a regression introduced by the `Unlock()` refactoring in dotnet/wpf#4425.

## Testing

Demo test: https://github.com/lindexi/lindexi_gd/tree/82c1dc09816d7a15214a167cae78f215a3393d6c/BitmapSourceTest

## Risk

Low. The change restores the original final-unlock guard without changing public APIs or single-lock behavior. The separation of unlocking from commit subscription introduced by the deadlock fix remains intact
